label: rem:q-flat-connection
title: The $d_q^2 \neq 0$ obstruction as curvature
html:
A q-flat connection carries the minimal possible curvature compatible with the q-deformation: curvature arising solely from the perpetual d_q^2 obstruction rather than from any connection form. It is not flat in the classical sense (\nabla_q^2 \neq 0 in general). When \kappa_0 \neq 0 (the perpetual obstruction), q-flat connections exist but have non-zero total curvature (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}.

The condition \nabla^2 = 0 provides the geometric incarnation of d^2 = 0. The q-flatness equation \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} absorbs the canonical obstruction to flatness. The Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg comparison (Kummer filtration) identifies the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} with the gerbe-theoretic obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m). The Kummer filtration pulls back to a filtration on HH^2 that measures the n-divisibility of the q-curvature.

The HKR identification. The Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg comparison (Kummer filtration) identifies the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q with the obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m). The deformation-theoretic obstruction HH^2 and the gerbe class in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) are two views of the same class. The Kummer filtration on the target pulls back to a filtration on HH^2 measuring n-divisibility of the q-curvature.

The perpetual obstruction and Hecke commutativity. From the Hecke perspective, the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q is the categorical shadow of the non-commutativity of Hecke operators at different places: classically Hecke operators at distinct points commute, but the q-deformation introduces (q-1)-proportional commutators. The perpetual obstruction (Kummer filtration) ensures this non-commutativity persists at cofinitely many Kummer levels.
